summary: Scene state is what a scene remembers beyond its text, kept so that regenerating, choosing a version, cutting, restoring and forking all leave it where the shown history says. A piece of state is a slot declared in one file and listed by a generator. What one reply version changed in a slot is a delta, a value at a path rather than an operation, stored on that version by swipe id so a fork shares its prefix's deltas without copying them. The state is rebuilt from the shown versions, from the nearest keyframe, inside the transaction of whatever changed the history. Phase 1 has one slot, the macro variables, and two slot families for the library trackers a scene links, whose state a tracker's update tool writes as pending deltas on the reply being written. Its sections cover slots, deltas and the three strategies, storage, rebuild, how a turn uses it (with the variables route and the chat import), what is tested, and what is not built yet. A range read of the same data shows what each message changed.
topics: macro variables as the first slot

sections.title: Slots
sections.summary: A slot is one file under src/core/scene-state/slots that exports defineSlot with an id, a scope, a diff strategy and a default. defineSlot refuses an id outside the allowed pattern and a keyed-list without a key. The command bun run slots writes the generated list from the folder, slots:check fails when it is stale, and a completeness test fails when a slot file is missing from the list or an id repeats. The only scope is scene, meaning rebuilt from history. The one slot so far, vars, uses the fields strategy, so each variable keeps the time it was first written and the time it was last written, which is exactly what the macro engine's variable record holds. Its family form, for state made by library pieces, is the child section below.

children.title: Slot families
children.summary: A slot id ending in a colon and a star is a family covering every id with that prefix, so state made by a library piece at run time needs no file of its own and the store never sees library pieces. The slot lookup gives the exact slot if there is one, else the family whose prefix the id has. A family id is one lowercase word, a colon and a star; its file is named without them, and overlapping or repeated families fail the generator. Two exist, tracker-record with the fields strategy and tracker-list with the keyed-list strategy keyed by name; a tracker's own value shape is checked in the core tracker module.

sections.title: Deltas and the three strategies
sections.summary: A delta names a slot, a path inside it, a value or a removal marker, and the time of the write. It is always a value, never an operation, so cutting a middle message takes back exactly what that message set and nothing a later message set again. Three strategies cut and fold deltas: value keeps the whole value, fields keeps one delta per named field, and keyed-list keeps one delta per row found by a key field. Only fields is used so far, though all three are implemented and tested. Fold skips a delta for an unknown slot or with a path its strategy cannot read, and the stores refuse such a delta outright. A variable named like an Object property is an ordinary own property.

sections.title: Storage
sections.summary: Migration 43 adds five tables and an index. swipe_deltas holds one row per delta keyed by swipe id and sequence and is never changed once written, so a fork that keeps swipe ids shares its prefix's deltas. message_deltas holds what a message carries whichever version shows, such as a person's edit on a reply, and a fork copies it with the new message id. branch_base is what a take starts with before any message, an import's variables, and is real data that refuses when damaged. branch_state is each take's tip cache, and state_keyframes keeps the whole state after every fiftieth shown message. Both are caches that every change rewrites, and a cache cell that will not open is rebuilt, never fatal. Paths, values, the base, keyframe and tip states and pending deltas are sealed like other chat payloads; slot, removal flag and time stay readable. The tables join the row fingerprints, the health check and the snapshot lists. A version has no size cap on its deltas; only what an import or a person's edit brings meets a hostile-input ceiling.

sections.title: Rebuild
sections.summary: The store owns the rebuild and runs it inside the transaction of the change, so no caller can forget it. It starts from the nearest kept keyframe on the shown path, else the take's base, else nothing, folds the deltas of the shown versions after it in order, rewrites the keyframes it passes and writes the tip cache. Committing a reply, adding or choosing a version, and cutting or restoring each rebuild from the message they changed; a fork rebuilds the new take, and deleting a take drops its cache. A continue stamps no delta, and a failed turn has stamped nothing. sceneStateBefore answers what a new version of a message builds from. sceneDeltas is a range read of the same data: the state before the first message without its own deltas, and each live message's deltas in fold order, changing nothing.

sections.title: How a turn uses it
sections.summary: loadTurn reads the variables from sceneState for a new reply and from sceneStateBefore for a new version or a continue, so a regenerate never counts its own earlier writes twice. Assembly returns the local variable changes, and scene-turn turns them into vars deltas saved on the checkpoint with the trace; commitTurn stamps them on the version it stores and rebuilds the take. A continue makes no deltas. That save is awaited and waits up to 30 seconds for the write lock, so a lost save cannot commit a reply without its variables, and a turn's deltas are never refused for size. Global variables are untouched. The variables route reads the vars slot, and a chat import records its variables as the take's base. The trackers' update tool adds deltas mid-reply through the turn's one door, for tracker slots only, as the one stateScoped write. A write of a value the message already shows, its version's deltas included, adds nothing, so a person's tracker edit back to the value before a reply is kept on the tip message.

sections.title: Not built yet
sections.summary: Everything past the first slot is planned in the scene-state plan and absent from the code. That covers more slots such as the Spellbook, the summary, the Props trackers and the Director's rounds, global variables as a derived log, the Compendium's shared lane, writer classes and permissions, the Story Director updating library trackers, hand edits of any slot other than a library tracker's, and a state inspector. recordMessageDeltas is the store's door for a write that is not a turn's; its one caller is the person's tracker edit from the Messenger's Trackers panel. This section exists so that no reader takes a planned part of the design for current behavior.

sections.title: What is tested
sections.summary: Unit tests prove each strategy's diff, fold with removal markers, and a rebuild from a keyframe equal to one from nothing. The ChatStore contract suite runs for both stores and covers choosing, cutting and restoring versions, a restore as a new take, a fork, dropped, committed and continued turns, refusals, and a two thousand message rebuild. A separate contract file holds the range read to both stores, including a person's edit on the first message of a range. A SQLite test adds the file-only facts: shared delta rows, keyframes, sealing, and a dense rebuild held to a two hundred millisecond budget. A busy-library test runs a real turn with the lock held, the turn tests prove a prompt's increment counts once, and a guard test fails when code outside the SQLite chat store names the tables.
